An AI just rewrote another AI's brain. No training involved. 🤯

MIT CSAIL researchers call it Weight-Space Programming: a frontier LLM (GPT-6 Astra) reads a model's raw weights, works out what they do, and edits them directly. No gradient descent.

What it pulled off:
→ Changed just 0.016% of a small Qwen model's weights and fixed its reasoning loops. Its math score jumped from 8% to 48%
→ Started from all zeros and wrote a Breakout-playing network from scratch. It scored 517. A normally trained model got 25 after 500 million steps

It's still early, but we might soon program models instead of training them.

Credit: Rikiya Takehi, Jayden Teoh, Alex Zhang & Omar Khattab (MIT CSAIL)

transkript.t: There's a new MIT research paper called Weight Space Programming,
and it shows an AI can write another AI's weights without any training.
Normally, every model is trained with gradient descent,
but here, an LLM just reads the raw numbers, figures out what they do, and edits them directly.
They gave it a small quen model stuck in reasoning loops,
and by changing just 0.016% of its weights,
its math score jumped from 8% to 48%.
it wrote a breakout playing network from scratch that scored 517,
while a normally trained model, after 500 million steps, scored 25.
It's still early, but we might soon program models instead of training them.
